name: Congenital Primary Aphakia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Primary Aphakia

criteria.description: Complete absence of the crystalline lens confirmed by clinical examination and imaging
Presence of anterior segment malformations such as microcornea or shallow anterior chamber
Identification of mutations in genes associated with lens development (e.g., FOXE3 gene mutations)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Complete absence of the crystalline lens on clinical and imaging evaluation plus presence of anterior segment abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Aplasia/Hypoplasia affecting the anterior segment of the eye

common.symptomName: Anterior synechiae of the anterior chamber

imaging: Ultrasound biomicroscopy demonstrating absence of lens
B-scan ocular ultrasound confirming absence of crystalline lens
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing anterior segment malformations
other: Clinical slit-lamp examination revealing aphakia and anterior segment anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: History of surgical removal or trauma to the lens
Later onset compared to congenital primary aphakia
Presence of lens may be normal or abnormal but not completely absent
Broader spectrum of anterior segment anomalies

redFlags: Complete absence of lens on imaging in a newborn
Severe visual impairment or blindness at birth
Associated anterior segment malformations increasing risk of glaucoma
references: Shastry BS. Congenital primary aphakia: a rare developmental anomaly. Indian J Ophthalmol. 2014.
Khan AO. Congenital primary aphakia: clinical and genetic aspects. Ophthalmic Genet. 2017.
